questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: What is the primary role of an operating system kernel?

options.text: To act as the core interface between hardware and software processes
To compile high-level programming code into assembly
To provide a visual graphic user interface directly
To encrypt hard disk drives by default

questions.explanation: The kernel is the core component of an OS that manages system resources and communications between hardware and software components.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: Which CPU scheduling algorithm may lead to starvation of processes with longer burst times?
questions.explanation: Shortest Job First (SJF) can cause starvation if short processes keep arriving, delaying long processes indefinitely.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: Which of the following are necessary conditions for a deadlock to occur? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Coffman's 4 conditions: Mutual exclusion, Hold & wait, No preemption, and Circular wait.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: Virtual memory allows an execution of processes that may not be completely in physical memory.
questions.explanation: Virtual memory separates user logical memory from physical memory, enabling execution of partially loaded processes.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: What is "Belady's Anomaly" in operating systems?

options.text: CPU utilization decreases when more processes are added
Page fault rate increases as number of allocated page frames increases
Disk access times double during heavy fragmentation
Deadlocks cannot be resolved by terminating a single process

questions.explanation: Beladys anomaly is the phenomenon in which increasing the number of page frames results in an increase in the number of page faults for certain memory access patterns (commonly in FIFO).

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: A binary semaphore initialized to 1 can be used to achieve:
questions.explanation: A binary semaphore has values 0 or 1 and behaves like a mutex to ensure only one thread or process enters the critical section.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: What is the term for a process that has completed execution but still has an entry in the process table?
questions.explanation: A zombie process or defunct process is a process that has finished execution via exit() but whose entry remains in the process table to report status to the parent.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: In Unix-like systems, which data structure contains metadata about a file except its name and actual content?
questions.explanation: An inode (index node) stores attributes and disk block locations of file system objects.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: Threads within the same process share the same heap memory and global variables.
questions.explanation: Threads share the text segment, data segment, and OS resources, but maintain private stacks and program counters.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.questionText: Explain the difference between Monolithic Kernels and Microkernels, citing advantages and trade-offs of each architecture.
questions.explanation: Monolithic kernels run all OS services (file system, VFS, drivers, IPC) in kernel space for high performance, whereas microkernels run only essential primitives (IPC, low-level memory, scheduling) in kernel space and move other services to user space for fault tolerance and modularity.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort?
questions.explanation: QuickSort exhibits O(N^2) in the worst case when the chosen pivot is repeatedly the smallest or largest element.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.questionText: In an AVL tree, what is the maximum allowed difference between the heights of left and right subtrees of any node?
questions.explanation: An AVL tree is a self-balancing BST where the balance factor (height(left) - height(right)) must be in {-1, 0, 1}.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.questionText: Which algorithm is used to find the shortest path from a single source in a graph with non-negative edge weights?
questions.explanation: Dijkstras algorithm finds shortest paths from a single source vertex to all other vertices in graphs with non-negative edge weights.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.questionText: A Queue follows the Last In First Out (LIFO) principle.
questions.explanation: A Queue follows First In First Out (FIFO). Stacks follow LIFO.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.questionText: Which of the following are collision resolution techniques in hash tables?
questions.explanation: Separate chaining, linear probing, quadratic probing, and double hashing are collision resolution techniques. Huffman is for data compression.

questions.subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
questions.questionText: Which divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm guarantees O(N log N) time complexity in all cases (worst, average, best)?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort always takes O(N log N) time because it splits the array in half and takes linear time to merge.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.questionText: What does the "I" in ACID properties of transactions stand for?
questions.explanation: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.questionText: A relation is in 3NF if it is in 2NF and there is no:

options.text: Transitive dependency of non-prime attributes on candidate keys

questions.explanation: Third Normal Form (3NF) requires 2NF and no transitive dependency where X -> Y and Y -> Z for non-prime attributes.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.questionText: A table in a relational database can have multiple Clustered Indexes.
questions.explanation: Because a clustered index determines the physical storage order of the rows, there can be only one clustered index per table.

questions.subject: Database Management Systems
questions.questionText: Which SQL JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right table, filling nulls where no match exists?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN returns all records from left table and matching rows from right table, defaulting missing values to NULL.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.questionText: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for reliable process-to-process packet delivery and flow control?
questions.explanation: The Transport layer (Layer 4) provides end-to-end communication services for applications, including connection-oriented data stream support, reliability, flow control, and multiplexing.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.questionText: Which of the following protocols operate over UDP by default?
questions.explanation: DNS queries, DHCP, and TFTP use UDP. HTTP/1.1 runs over TCP.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.questionText: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits in length.
questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128-bit (16-byte) addresses, written in 8 groups of 4 hexadecimal digits.

questions.subject: Digital Electronics
questions.questionText: Which logic gate produces a HIGH output only when both of its inputs are different?
questions.explanation: Exclusive-OR (XOR) gives true output if and only if one input is true and the other false.

questions.subject: Digital Electronics
questions.questionText: What is the condition called when J=1 and K=1 in a JK Flip-Flop, causing output toggle at each clock pulse?
questions.explanation: When both J and K are high, the output toggles with each active clock transition.

questions.subject: Thermodynamics
questions.questionText: Which law of thermodynamics defines the concept of temperature and thermal equilibrium?
questions.explanation: The Zeroth law states that if two systems are in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other, defining temperature.

questions.subject: Thermodynamics
questions.questionText: The efficiency of a reversible Carnot engine operating between temperatures Th and Tc is:
questions.explanation: Carnot efficiency eta = 1 - Tc / Th, where temperatures are in Kelvin.
